primary_sources.title: Gerald Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, second edition
primary_sources.reviewed: Section 2.3, Theorems 2.13-2.14 and the positive nonclosable point-evaluation example.
primary_sources.access: Direct PDF opens returned HTTP 502. The author-hosted indexed passages, including Theorem 2.13 and its proof, were retrieved by targeted web search. The second primary source below was opened directly.
primary_sources.use: Standard Friedrichs and closed-form framework; a symmetric operator mapping its core into the Hilbert space is required, not just positivity of an abstract form.

primary_sources.title: Ashbaugh et al., Spectral Theory for Perturbed Krein Laplacians in Nonsmooth Domains
primary_sources.reviewed: Section 2, equations (2.14)-(2.21): intrinsic Friedrichs domain, form closure and preservation of constant shifts.
primary_sources.access: Author-hosted PDF opened; exact relevant passages reviewed.
primary_sources.use: Independent directly accessible account of the established extension construction. Its domain-specific spectral theorems are not transferred to the wormhole.

strongest_comparator: The immediately preceding whole-exterior full thermal coercivity theorem on the compact shape core and its stronger completion. The earlier normal-model inverse does not establish the charged full operator's domain.
new_consequence: A closed full thermal form in its own norm and a Friedrichs inverse bounded by 40G/gamma^2 in L2_w, with source-response estimates and global conformal reconstruction norm below 4/5.
hardest_step: Prove that the actual canonical row and both reconstructed local Euler rows map every compact shape input into L2_w. The global geodesic point action, actual anchored remainder contacts, endpoint local jets and bounded adjoint reconstruction provide this mapping.
novelty_scope: Charged-seed domain application and bounded reconstruction; no new abstract Friedrichs, Hardy or logarithmic theorem.
verification_scope: Exact graph/adjoint identities and endpoint Weyl Euler rows, independent normal-form quadrature, and refined charged reconstruction/adjoint solves. Continuum operator membership and closure remain ordinary proofs.
